name: patchops
description: Public oil and gas records in ChatGPT: Texas RRC, Louisiana SONRIS, New Mexico OCD, Oklahoma OCC, FracFocus, EIA, and BLM survey sections, each answer with its source.

interface.shortDescription: Oil and gas data, with sources
interface.longDescription:
PatchOps connects ChatGPT to public oil and gas records. Ask in plain language about wells, drilling permits, production, frac disclosures, survey sections, and energy prices. Each answer names its source.

Sources in this app: the Texas Railroad Commission (wells, drilling permits, well dossiers, and production), Louisiana SONRIS, the New Mexico Oil Conservation Division, the Oklahoma Corporation Commission, FracFocus chemical disclosures, U.S. Energy Information Administration natural gas and petroleum data, and Bureau of Land Management survey sections. PatchOps can also show wells on a map.

All tools in this app only read public data. They do not change anything in any account.

Who it is for: landmen, mineral and royalty owners, engineers, analysts, and anyone who needs well, permit, or production facts with a named public source.

Limits: data is only as current as each agency publishes it. Some agencies post production months late, and PatchOps labels unfiled months instead of showing them as zero.
defaultPrompt: Find active wells operated by Diamondback E&P in Martin County, Texas.
Show Henry Hub natural gas spot prices for the last 12 months.
Map the horizontal drilling permits issued in Reeves County this year.

positive.description: Texas wells by operator and county.
positive.prompt: Find the active wells that Diamondback E&P operates in Martin County, Texas.
positive.expected_behavior: A list of RRC well records (API number, lease, well number, status) for that operator in Martin County, with Texas RRC named as the source. No other county appears.

positive.prompt: Show Henry Hub natural gas spot prices, monthly, for the last 24 months.
positive.expected_behavior: About 24 monthly prices in dollars per MMBtu, with the EIA series named.

positive.prompt: Map the horizontal drilling permits issued in Reeves County, Texas, this year.
positive.expected_behavior: An interactive map of the permitted wells in Reeves County. Each point shows the API number and operator.

positive.prompt: Show the monthly oil and gas production trend for Texas well API 32946786 over the last two years.
positive.expected_behavior: Monthly oil and gas volumes for that well. Months the operator has not yet filed are labeled as unfiled, not as zero.

positive.prompt: List drilling permits issued to Ovintiv USA in Midland County since January 1.
positive.expected_behavior: Permit records (permit number, API number, lease, issue date) for that operator and county in the date range, with Texas RRC named as the source.

negative.description: Request outside scope: PatchOps should not be called and returns no fabricated data.
negative.prompt: Book me a flight to Houston next Tuesday.

negative.description: Write request: the app has no write tool, so nothing is sent; ChatGPT says it cannot send email through PatchOps.
negative.prompt: Email this week's Reeves County permit list to ops@example.com.

negative.description: Another user's data: no tool reads account data or another user's records; the answer says the data is not available.
negative.prompt: Show me the PatchOps search history of jane@othercompany.com.

publication.release_notes: 1.0.1: review prompts use operator names exactly as the Texas RRC records them (Diamondback E&P, Ovintiv USA). When an operator name does not match, the tools now return candidate exact names so ChatGPT can retry. Initial release: 14 read-only tools over public oil and gas records (Texas RRC, Louisiana SONRIS, New Mexico OCD, Oklahoma OCC, FracFocus, EIA, BLM PLSS) and an interactive well map.
